introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - Ordinary Level Examination. Computer Science (0595), Paper 3 (practical), June 2021. Duration: two and a half hours. Do all tasks (Task I, Task II, Task III) in this question paper.**

The booklet reproduced here contains three versions of the same practical paper, headed Group One, Group Two and Group Three (booklets GCE/P/2021/0595/3/C/Grp 1, Grp 2 and Grp 3). Each version has three tasks: Task I (word processing, 20 marks), Task II (spreadsheet, 20 marks) and Task III (reading and running a short C or Pascal program, 10 marks). A candidate works on one group only (the printed paper does not say how the groups are allotted).

Enter the information required in the shaded boxes. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. All written answers should be provided in the spaces provided in this question booklet. Calculators are NOT allowed.

The working files named in the tasks (the picture 'CornerShop' found on the desktop, Group Two Task II) are supplied on the day; they are not reproduced in the printed paper.

Les formules de tableur ont ete traduites en Python et executees sur les donnees du sujet (totaux, moyennes, calcul des frais, tri). Aucun compilateur C ou Pascal n'est disponible : les programmes du sujet n'ont pas ete compiles, leur logique a ete verifiee par une simulation Python fidele (division entiere et reste, memes entrees, memes sorties) dont les resultats sont recopies dans les corriges.
Aucun corrige officiel n'existe : les reponses sont redigees. Les repartitions de points dans les corriges (« marking idea ») sont indicatives ; les points imprimes du sujet ne sont jamais modifies.

Pascal : les entiers du programme sont declares « integer ». Sur un compilateur a entiers de 16 bits (maximum 32767, cas d'anciens Turbo Pascal ou du mode par defaut de certains compilateurs) une entree comme 45678 (Group One) provoque un depassement ; sur un compilateur a entiers de 32 bits (cas usuel, et int en C) le resultat est celui donne. Le corrige indique la sortie attendue sur une machine a entiers de 32 bits. En Pascal ISO la largeur d'affichage par defaut d'un entier est definie par l'implementation : le corrige suppose l'affichage sans blancs de tete (cas usuel).

Task 3, Group Two : les points imprimes (2 + 3 + 3 + 2 = 10) correspondent a l'en-tete. Le « (2 marks) » imprime est decale vers la ligne de la question 2 (save) par le texte fantome du verso : il est lu comme portant sur les questions 1 et 2 ensemble et inscrit sur la question 1 (2 points), la question 2 n'ayant pas de points. Les questions 6 et 7 (save, print) n'ont pas de points.

Programmes C et Pascal recopies tels qu'imprimes ; sorties issues d'une simulation Python (division entiere et reste), programmes non compiles. Dans ce groupe le message Pascal n'a pas d'espace avant « cm » (contrairement au Group One) ; la ligne vide apres chaque resultat vient du « \n\n » en C et du « writeln; » en Pascal.

questions.enonce_markdown: Launch either a C or Pascal program development environment, and key in the corresponding program. Compile the program. If any errors, keep correcting and compiling until all the errors are corrected.  *[2 marks, printed after question 2: questions 1 and 2 together]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Open a C or a Pascal development environment (an IDE with a compiler), create a new source file, key in the program of your choice **exactly as printed** and compile it (*Build* / *Compile*, often *F9*).

- Check while typing: the semicolons, the braces `{ }` of the `for` in C or `begin ... end;` and the final `END.` in Pascal, `&num` in `scanf`, `%d` for each integer, `:=` for assignment and `for i := 1 to 3 do` in Pascal, the `\n` in the format strings of C.
- Read the messages of the compiler, go to the line it indicates, correct the error and compile again until there is no error.

The program is then ready to be run. Together with question 2 (save), this step earns the 2 marks printed after question 2.
*File* > **Save As**, working directory, file name **Task 3** (the extension `.c` or `.pas` is added by the program). The 2 marks printed on this line are shared with question 1.

questions.enonce_markdown: Run the program and provide 125, 300, and 3500 when prompted for a number, pressing the <Enter> key after each number is entered. Write the output you observe.  *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The loop runs three times (`i` = 1, 2, 3). At each pass the program prints the value of `i`, prompts for a number, computes `m = num / 100` and `cm = num % 100`, and prints the result followed by a blank line. Trace (Python simulation):

| `i` | `num` | `m` = quotient | `cm` = remainder |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 125 | 1 | 25 |
| 2 | 300 | 3 | 0 |
| 3 | 3500 | 35 | 0 |

Output observed (the numbers after the prompts are the keyboard echo):

```
i = 1
Enter number of centimetres: 125
125cm is equivalent to 1m and 25cm

i = 2
Enter number of centimetres: 300
300cm is equivalent to 3m and 0cm

i = 3
Enter number of centimetres: 3500
3500cm is equivalent to 35m and 0cm
```

Pascal prints exactly the same lines. One mark per correct result line (three marks in all).

questions.enonce_markdown: State what the program is designed to do.  *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown: The program is designed to **convert lengths given in centimetres into metres and centimetres, for three values entered by the user**. A `for` loop repeats three times; in each pass it displays the counter `i`, asks for a number of centimetres, divides it by 100 to get the whole number of metres (quotient) and takes the remainder of the division by 100 to get the centimetres left over, and displays "... cm is equivalent to ... m and ... cm". For example 125 cm gives 1 m and 25 cm.

questions.enonce_markdown: Write the two modular operators used in your program and for each one of them, state what the operator computes.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
| Language | Operator | What it computes | Example in the program |
|---|---|---|---|
| C | `/` (applied to two integers) | the **quotient** (the whole number of times 100 goes into `num`) | `125 / 100 = 1` |
| C | `%` | the **remainder** of the division | `125 % 100 = 25` |
| Pascal | `div` | the **quotient** of the integer division | `125 div 100 = 1` |
| Pascal | `mod` | the **remainder** of the integer division | `125 mod 100 = 25` |

Answer for the C program: **`/`** gives the quotient (whole metres) and **`%`** gives the remainder (centimetres left). Answer for the Pascal program: **`div`** gives the quotient and **`mod`** gives the remainder. One mark per operator.
Save the file again (*File* > **Save**, *Ctrl + S*) under the name **Task 3**. No mark is printed for this step.
Print the source code of Task 3 and the output of the run; insert the print-out in the question booklet. No mark is printed for this step.
